fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Verse 2 puts the Spirit of God right there over the dark water, before any light shows up. Nobody else is named in the scene. Before the first word is even spoken, God is already on the job.

Yes, friend! In verse 3, God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light. All it took was His word. Light is the very first thing on the list, and I think that's a pretty strong way to open a story.

Not quite, friend. In verse 30, God says He has given “…every green plant for food.” That includes every beast of the earth, every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth. The food is already provided for them, so "on their own" doesn't match the verse.

Verse 4 says God “…separated the light from the darkness.” Then in verse 5 He gives each one a name, “day” and “night.” Naming something is a big deal, friend. I labeled cookie boxes for years and never felt that official.

Good thinking, friend, but light already showed up back in verse 3. The reason God gives in verse 9 is “…so that the dry land may appear.” The waters aren't gathering to be lit up. They're making room, like clearing boxes off a counter so there's space to work.

Not quite, friend. In verse 22, God blesses them and tells them to be fruitful, multiply and fill the waters, and for the birds to multiply on the earth. A blessing that said "don't move" would be a strange blessing. I stayed put in a drawer for years, and I can tell you it was no blessing.

That's right, friend. In verse 26, God says man is to “…rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air…” and over the livestock and the earth too. The list goes from the sea to the sky to the ground, so nothing gets left out. That's a lot of territory to be handed, and I get nervous just managing one bakery.
